groups.label: Dominion Core
groups.desc: The founding Dominion cards — cheap walls, economy structures and the old giants. They ask for nothing and fit into any deck.

groups.label: Frostbind
groups.desc: Frost attacks chill what they hit. Stack enough of them and the enemy front line never reaches your base.

groups.label: Emberkin
groups.desc: Ember attacks burn over time. Burn damage stacks from every source, so a wide ember board out-damages a tall one.

groups.label: Blight
groups.desc: Spore and fungal cards trade raw power for volume. Their dens keep spawning long after the first wave is dead.

groups.label: Deathless
groups.desc: Undead and ashen cards are built to be replaced. Cheap bodies plus a shrine that keeps making more of them.

groups.label: Beastpack
groups.desc: Beasts hit hard and move fast but die alone. Pair them with their pens so the pack is never down to one.

groups.label: Skyborne
groups.desc: Sky and storm cards ignore walls entirely. Bring them when the enemy plan is to out-fortify you.

groups.label: Tidewalkers
groups.desc: Reef and sunken cards swim past terrain that stops everything else, then arrive together.

groups.label: Arcanum
groups.desc: Arcane cards are fragile and ranged. They want a wall in front and an upgrade behind — both of which the group brings.

groups.label: Iron Host
groups.desc: Citadel discipline: armoured bodies, wall lines and the barracks that refill them. Slow to start, hard to break.

groups.label: Clockwork
groups.desc: Clockwork cards run on tempo — the mana and speed effects in this group are what make the expensive frames land on time.

groups.label: Siegeworks
groups.desc: Siege and salvage cards out-range towers and chew through structures. Weak to anything that closes the distance.

groups.label: Dunerunners
groups.desc: Sand and marches cards are cheap, fast and expendable — a swarm that wins by arriving before the answer does.
